title: Seattle Travel Guide

hero.headline: Seattle Travel Guide
hero.subheadline: Plan a high-value Seattle itinerary with top neighborhoods, outdoor access, and proven tour ideas.

overview: Seattle is a strong base for culture, food, and outdoor day plans. Build each day around one anchor area, then add nearby experiences to reduce transit time.
For first-time visitors, pair iconic landmarks with one local neighborhood each day. This gives you a more complete feel for Seattle without over-scheduling.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Seattle Waterfront
thingsToDo.description: Seattle's central waterfront runs along Elliott Bay from Pioneer Square toward Belltown and includes major public assets like Pike Place Market access points, the Seattle Aquarium, and Pier 57. The district has undergone a large post-viaduct rebuild tied to Waterfront Park projects, expanding pedestrian promenades and connecting downtown to the bay.

bestTimeToVisit.title: Shoulder seasons are best for comfort and flexibility
bullets: Spring and fall typically offer the easiest weather for walking and tours.
Summer can be busy; reserve major attractions and timed entries early.
Winter trips can provide better rates and lighter midday crowds in many districts.

travelTips: Use early starts for major sights and popular viewpoints.
Pre-book top attractions and guided activities during peak months.
Keep one flexible block each day for weather or traffic changes.
Stay close to transit hubs if you want to minimize transfer time.

faq.q: How many days are ideal for Seattle?
faq.a: Three to four days gives enough time for major attractions and one outdoor-focused day.

faq.q: Is Seattle good for outdoor travelers?
faq.a: Yes. Most itineraries can combine city highlights with nearby hiking, water, or scenic touring options.

faq.q: Should I book tours in advance?
faq.a: For top-rated tours and peak travel weeks, advance booking is strongly recommended.
